newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: Ethiopia raises oil products prices.
newsitem.headline: Ethiopia raises oil products prices.

text.p: Ethiopia has increased prices on most refined oil products, the ministry of trade and industry said on Monday. The changes were effective on Sunday.

The ministry said the increase was made necessary by a 23 percent rise in the price of crude oil which jumped from $17 to $21 per barrel in the internaitonal market and as a result of the weakening of the Ethiopian birr currency.
The ministry said in a statement that the price of regular petrol in the capital Addis Ababa would be $0.37 (birr 2.33) per litre from $0.31 (birr 2.00) previously.
The price increase varied from place to place depending on the distance between customers and the port of entry of the feul into Ethiopia -- currently the Eritrean port of Assab.

The highest price for a litre of regular petrol after the adjustments would be in the remote western region of Dembio Dolo, at $0.40 (2.50) per litre while the lowest will be $0.34 (birr 2.19) per litre at Tendaho in the Afar Region near Assab.
The price of a litre of kerosene, a product much used by people in the low income bracket for cooking and for lamps, jumped from $0.16 (birr 1.00) to $0.20 (birr 1.25) per litre.
The price of butane gas, used by diplomats and the wealthy, was also increased to $7.93 (birr 50.50) from $5.80 (birr 37) per cylinder at retailers.
